question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Lineage barcoding plus scRNA-seq to trace survivor origin
ideas.description: Label each cell with a heritable barcode before treatment, then compare barcode frequencies and transcriptomes of survivors to pre-treatment clones. This shows whether survivors were pre-existing lineages with a stable state or arose from induced switching in cells that were not previously distinguished.

ideas.title: Pre-treatment live-cell reporter tracking linked to fate
ideas.description: Track individual cells with a cell-cycle or stress reporter before drug addition, then add the drug and follow each cell to death or survival. Matching pre-treatment reporter state to eventual fate tests whether slow cycling or a specific pre-drug state predicts survival.

ideas.title: Per-cell drug accumulation and efflux measurement
ideas.description: Quantify intracellular drug levels in individual cells with a fluorescent analog, or in sorted subpopulations by LC-MS, and relate them to survival. This tests whether differences in uptake, efflux, or sequestration, rather than target biology, explain why some cells escape.

ideas.title: Sort-and-replate memory and heritability assay
ideas.description: Sort cells defined by a survival-linked reporter before treatment, re-expose them to drug, and measure how well the survival phenotype is inherited across divisions and after drug withdrawal. Heritable survival points to a stable epigenetic or regulatory memory, while loss on replating points to transient tolerance.

ideas.title: Endogenous target-abundance and noise profiling
ideas.description: Tag the drug target at its endogenous locus and quantify per-cell target protein levels and their variability before treatment. Testing whether cells with low target abundance or high expression noise are preferentially spared identifies a dose-target stoichiometry mechanism that could be therapeutically exploited.

candidates: Lineage barcoding (CellTag/LARRY) with scRNA-seq to see whether survivors derive from pre-existing clones or arise from induced switching
Time-resolved scRNA-seq during early drug exposure to catch transient adaptive states before survivors stabilize
Live-cell FUCCI or cell-cycle reporter tracking before drug addition, linked to single-cell fate (survive or die)
ScATAC-seq or chromatin accessibility profiling before treatment to find primed regions that predict survival
Sort-and-replate memory test: sort reporter-defined survivor-like cells, re-expose to drug, and measure heritability and reversibility
Drug holiday / pulse-withdrawal experiments to separate reversible tolerance from stable, heritable resistance
Per-cell intracellular drug quantification with fluorescent analogs or sorted-cell LC-MS to test pharmacokinetic heterogeneity
Efflux transporter (ABCB1, ABCG2) reporter sorting combined with drug accumulation assays
Endogenous tagging of the drug target to quantify per-cell target abundance and noise versus survival
Pooled CRISPR screen with single-cell readout to find genes that shift survival probability, not just IC50
CRISPRi or CRISPRa perturbation of top predictive pre-treatment genes to test causality
TMRM or NAD(P)H autofluorescence sorting to test whether mitochondrial or metabolic state predicts survival
Mass cytometry or phosphoflow of signaling nodes before treatment to find pre-existing pathway heterogeneity
Phosphoproteomics of sorted pre-treatment subpopulations to compare signaling networks
Single-cell DNA sequencing or karyotyping to test whether aneuploidy or copy-number variation predicts survival
Duplex sequencing of survivors to detect rare pre-existing mutations and separate them from nongenetic tolerance
Fluctuation (Luria-Delbruck) assays combined with barcoding to quantify mutational versus nongenetic routes to survival
Extrachromosomal DNA FISH per cell to test whether ecDNA copy number underlies drug tolerance
Spatial imaging of survivors within colonies to test whether position, density, or cell contact predicts survival
Co-culture or conditioned-medium experiments to test whether neighboring cells or secreted factors protect survivors
